claim: The book teaches 毎年 with two readings, まいねん／まいとし, but the card's back shows only the first, so the learner never meets まいとし and one who reads it maitoshi (natural after 今年 kotoshi) is told nothing that confirms it.
evidence: Learner: Reading BACK: '毎年 / Answer: Every year / Says: mainen'. The card's reviewNote (not shown on the face): 'The book gives more than one reading: まいねん, まいとし. Audio uses the first.' From 今年 'kotoshi' the learner can equally reach まいとし. Reader: Book, kanji 068 毎: "毎年(まいねん／まいとし) every year". Card r-4d564a3bda7f: target 毎年, English "Every year", Says "mainen", reviewNote "The book gives more than one reading: まいねん, まいとし. Audio uses the first."
fix: Show both readings on the back ("mainen / maitoshi"), keeping the audio on the first.
verdictReason: Facts verified: the kanji table (21.xhtml, entry 068 毎) prints "毎年(まいねん／まいとし) every year"; cards.json has ttsText まいねん, pronunciation "mainen" and the reviewNote both roles quote, and the rendered back says only "Says: mainen". But this is the deck-wide convention, not a slip on this card: six cards in the collection carry the identical reviewNote (十歳 ch-16, 十分 ch-19, 七人, 男の人, 女の人 ch-8, 毎年), no word card anywhere shows two romaji readings (only silent kanji cards do), docs/designs/reading-decks/04-card-rules.md says the romaji is made from the word's reading, singular, and build-reading-deck SKILL.md says the audio uses the first reading. Same ruling as chapter-8/r-e9d3dae7d71d (七人). What settles it: the owner ruling already requested there, on whether a word card's Says line may list the book's alternative readings when the audio voices the first; if yes, apply to all six at once, if no, close as wont-fix. Severity stays polish.

claim: The gloss 'Entry to a company' reads like a physical way in, which matches the learner's 入口 'Entrance' and lets a wrong guess ('company entrance') feel confirmed.
evidence: Reading FRONT: '入社'. BACK: 'Answer: Entry to a company / Says: nyūsha'. Ledger: 入口 | Entrance; 入り口 | Entrance; 入る | To enter; 社 | Company.
fix: Gloss it as 'Joining a company' (or 'Joining a company (as an employee)').
verdictReason: The card copies the book's own gloss: the kanji table (entry 063 社) prints "入社(にゅうしゃ) entry to a company", and a faithful card whose wording looks odd is not a finding (qa/README.md; same ruling as chapter-7 曲がる "To turn" and chapter-11 暖かい "Warm"). Nothing collides with it either: 入口 (ch-11) and 入り口 (ch-19) answer "Entrance", not "Entry", and no other card in the collection answers "Entry to a company", so preflight's reading-distinct-english check passes. Rewording to "Joining a company" would move the card away from the book for a guess the learner has to unlearn anyway once the back is read.

claim: 文字 and the kanji card 字 give the same answer with the senses reordered, so the English does not tell the two cards apart (reading rule 9).
evidence: Card r-f4d3dab8e0c2 文字: "Letter; character" (book: "文字(もじ) letter; character"). Card chapter-7 字: "Character; letter" (KANJIDIC).
fix: Narrow one of them, for example 文字 "Letter; character (of a script)" or 字 "Character; letter (single written character)".
verdictReason: Not a collision under the deck's rule. card-rules-reading.md rule 9 forbids two WORDS or two CHARACTERS sharing an English answer, and preflight's reading-distinct-english check (src/audit/checks/reading.js:119) compares kanji cards with kanji cards and words with words by the owner's 2026-10-14 decision, because a kanji card's English is the kanji's own meaning and the word built on it naturally shares it. A collection-wide count finds 61 such character/word pairs already shipping and reviewed (食 "To eat" / 食べる, 小 "Small" / 小さい, 入 "To enter" / 入る, 社 "Company" / 会社, and so on), so this is a settled convention, not a defect of this card. Here 文字 "Letter; character" is the book's exact gloss (entry 070 文: "文字(もじ) letter; character") and chapter-7 字 "Character; letter" is a KANJIDIC2 character card (r-582c50066c2c, silent, reviewNote "Not taught by the book yet"), a different class; narrowing either would move the word away from the book or the kanji away from its source.
